model: Compartment model of Anderson-Howells-Rojas La Luz (2026) with no inflow, exit or coagulation; each compartment runs a two-species chemistry in S (substrate) and I (inhibitor); a compartment with s substrate molecules divides at rate lambda*s; one daughter keeps all S and, given a fresh Q in [0,1], each I independently with probability Q; minimal continuous-time Markov chain; explosion = infinitely many events in finite time.

claims.statement: If every reaction has S in its source complex and the kernel keeps all S in one daughter, the compartment model explodes iff the single active-compartment chain with export transitions at rate lambda*S(x) times the substrate-daughter kernel explodes.

Conversion inhibition (2S->3S at b s(s-1), S->S+I at c s, S+I->2I at d s i, d>b), fixed retention p, s0>=2: the isolated chemistry is nonexplosive; the compartment model explodes with positive probability iff d+lambda*log p<b (always if p=0); nonexplosive at equality and for p=1; P(T<inf | marked environment)=P(K<s0-1) with K a sum of independent Bernoulli(exp(-b tau_j)) over conversion times tau_j.
If Delta=b+lambda(1-p)-d>0 then P(T<inf)>=1-d(i0+c/b)/(Delta(s0-1)); equals 1/2 for b=c=1,d=2,lambda=3,p=0,(s0,i0)=(3,0).
Almost surely on explosion (conversion): (T-t)S(t)->1/b, C(t)/log(1/(T-t))->lambda/b, I_tot(t)/S(t)->0.

Catalytic inhibition (I+2S->I+S at d i s(s-1)): explosion with positive probability iff b*lambda*(1-p)>d*c; equality nonexplosive; P(T<inf | I)=1-(1-1/(b D_inf))^(s0-1); logarithmic blow-up asymptotics.
Random retention: conversion threshold d+lambda*E log Q<b (extended expectation, log 0=-inf); catalytic threshold b*lambda*(1-EQ)>dc; equality nonexplosive.

With an added well-mixed degradation S+I->S at delta s i: conversion threshold d-delta+lambda E log Q<b. Removing inhibitor at the same mean rate by degradation instead of division gives the strictly smaller explosive region lambda(1-EQ)>d-b; for catalysis the thresholds coincide.
Explosion probability is nonincreasing in coupled retention and nondecreasing in lambda, and tends to 0 as p increases to either critical value.
Conversion family: explosion with positive probability persists if each division may leak up to K substrate molecules, whenever d+lambda E log Q<b.
